task.description:
Review implementation of AGT-05, AGT-06, AGT-07 on branch feature/WF02-agt05-07-20260819 against security invariants in docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md.

Key invariants to check:
- Tenant data isolation: all artifact queries and scheduler sweeps include tenant scope (search_path or explicit predicate)
- SQL parameterisation: no string interpolation into queries
- No catch unreachable on realistic failures
- Field authorisation: no fields taken from request body without validation (artifact verify endpoint — who can call it?)
- Probe indistinguishability: deprecated field error (AGT-07) should not leak artifact existence

Run: git diff origin/main...feature/WF02-agt05-07-20260819 -- src/ migrations/

Return PASS or FAIL with specific invariant violations.

result.summary: Security review of AGT-05/06/07 on branch feature/WF02-agt05-07-20260819. All eight invariants assessed. No BLOCKER violations found.

invariant_assessment.INV-1: PASS — Migration 1173 creates tables under staging schema only (no public business tables). handleArtifactVerify scopes both UPDATE and fallback SELECT with tenant_id=$2::uuid; cross-tenant artifact_id is indistinguishable from non-existent (returns 404). Retention sweeps in artifact_retention.zig delete across all tenants — this is deliberate global maintenance on the shared staging schema, consistent with the pre-existing staging.* architecture (not per-tenant schemas). ADVISORY: retention sweeps carry implicit cross-tenant write authority; this is correct but should be documented as deliberate.
invariant_assessment.INV-2: PASS — handleArtifactVerify is accessible to any tenant-authenticated agent (actor_agent). No unauthorized response fields. task_spec_version/process_definition_version are stored as opaque text; no security-sensitive field exposure. ADVISORY: no per-agent ownership check — any agent in the tenant can verify any artifact in the same tenant. This appears intentional given the tenant-scoped isolation model.
invariant_assessment.INV-3: N/A — No new host API functions introduced in this diff.
invariant_assessment.INV-4: N/A — No secret material in diff. No new serialised structs containing secrets.
invariant_assessment.INV-5: PASS — The fallback exists_row query also filters by tenant_id=$2::uuid; a cross-tenant artifact_id returns null (404) identical to a non-existent artifact. Both cases return HTTP 404 with body shape {error:artifact_not_found,artifact_id:<caller-supplied>,status:404}. The echoed artifact_id is the caller's own input (not a server-retrieved value), so no existence information is leaked. AGT-07 deprecated-field check fires before any DB interaction — cannot leak artifact existence.
invariant_assessment.INV-6: SATISFIED — This handoff is the proof of scoping for all new data-access paths in this change.
invariant_assessment.INV-7: PASS — All new SQL uses $1/$2/$3 parameterized placeholders. TTL integer (days_str) is passed as a query parameter ($1::integer), not interpolated. grep for std.fmt.allocPrint with SQL keywords returned zero hits. No string interpolation into any query.
invariant_assessment.INV-8: PASS — grep for 'catch unreachable' in diff returned zero hits. Error handling uses typed propagation (!u64), catch return svc503(), and explicit catch |err| with std.log.err logging.

advisory_items.description: artifact_id is echoed in artifactNotFound404 response body via std.fmt.allocPrint. JSON injection is prevented in practice because an invalid UUID causes a DB cast error (svc503) before reaching the 404 path, but there is no explicit UUID format validation at the top of handleArtifactVerify. Consider adding an early-reject guard for defense-in-depth.

Retention sweeps (runArtifactRetentionSweep1/Sweep2) delete across all tenants without per-tenant scoping. Correct and intentional for global staging cleanup, but this cross-tenant write authority is not documented at the call site.
